q1: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S WHERE 0 = ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' )
q2: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON WHERE SALES_ID NOT IN (SELECT O.SALES_ID FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON C.COM_ID=O.COM_ID AND C.NAME='RED' )

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 finds salespersons who have zero orders associated with the company named 'RED'. Q2 finds salespersons whose SALES_ID does not appear in any order linked to the company named 'RED'. The difference arises when a salesperson has no orders at all (not just no orders for 'RED'). Q2 excludes such salespersons because their SALES_ID is not in the subquery result, while Q1 includes them since the count of orders for 'RED' is zero.
counterexample_dsp: A salesperson with no orders at all will be included in Q1's result but excluded from Q2's result because their SALES_ID is not in the subquery of Q2.
